vocabulary.definition: that, because (introduces ind. statement or cause)
I say (+ infinitive in ind. statement)

grammar.explanation: Relative pronouns agree with their antecedent in gender and number but take their case from their function in the relative clause. Greek has three constructions for indirect statement: ὅτι/ὡς + indicative, accusative + infinitive, and participle.

paradigms.name: Indirect Statement Constructions
rows: λέγει ὅτι ἔρχεται (he says that he is coming)
νομίζω αὐτὸν ἔρχεσθαι (I think him to be coming)
ὁρῶ αὐτὸν ἐρχόμενον (I see him coming)

rules: Relative attraction: relative assimilated to case of antecedent
ὅτι keeps original tense of direct statement
Infinitive tense = aspect (present ongoing, aorist simple)
Participle agrees with accusative subject in ind. statement

exercises.question: Translate: οἶδα ὅτι ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ ἥκει.
exercises.answer: I know that the Son of God has come.

exercises.question: Explain the attraction in: πάντων ὧν ἐποίησε
exercises.answer: ὧν (genitive) attracted from accusative ἅ to match antecedent πάντων: 'of all things which he did'

readingPassage.greek: Ἀκούομεν ὅτι ἔρχεται. Βλέπομεν αὐτὸν ἐρχόμενον. Πάντα ὅσα ἂν θέλητε ἵνα ποιῶσιν ὑμῖν οἱ ἄνθρωποι, οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς ποιεῖτε αὐτοῖς.
readingPassage.translation: We hear that he is coming. We see him coming. All things whatsoever you wish that people should do to you, so also you do to them.
